punchline: Shame grows in secrecy and silence, and it shrinks when you say it out loud to someone kind.
thirty_sec: Brené Brown distinguishes guilt from shame in Daring Greatly. Guilt says, 'I did something bad,' and can push you to repair things. Shame says, 'I am bad,' and pushes you to hide or blame. Shame, she writes, grows in secrecy, silence and judgment, and empathy is its antidote. Everyone feels it, but shame resilience, noticing it, questioning it and reaching out, can be learned.
question: After your last mistake, did your inner voice say 'I did something bad' or 'I am bad'?
